population.definition: Total resident population (de jure) of Port Louis District, 2022 Population Census (reference week ended 3 July 2022). The census tables show resident population unless stated. The Town of Port Louis has different boundaries: it includes areas in Moka and Black River districts; citypopulation.de lists the town at 140,403 (2022), but that figure was not checked in the official source.

source.title: 2022 Housing and Population Census, Volume III: Geographical and Migration Characteristics, Table G1
source.publisher: Statistics Mauritius (Ministry of Finance, Economic Planning and Development)
source.quote: PORT LOUIS DISTRICT-Wholly Urban 106,332

facts.claim: Construction of Port Louis began in 1735 under Mahé de La Bourdonnais, first governor of Mauritius; the site had been chosen as the island's port from 1732.

source.title: History - City Council Of Port Louis (History of the City)
source.quote: Bertrand François Mahé de Labourdonnais, the first governor of Mauritius, started the construction in 1735 (summary of page text; verify wording)

facts.claim: The city is named for King Louis XV of France; the French named the port and administrative centre Port Louis.

source.title: Port Louis, Mauritius (Research Starter)
source.author: Micah Issitt
source.quote: specifically named its primary port and administrative center Port Louis in honor of King

facts.claim: Dutch: the Dutch named the island for Prince Maurice of Nassau and founded the first permanent settlement in 1638, a timber community near the present city.

source.title: Port Louis, Mauritius (Research Starter)
source.author: Micah Issitt
source.quote: The Dutch named the island in honor of Dutch prince Maurice of Nassau.

facts.claim: French/British: the city carried other names under French rule (Port de La Montagne 1794, Port Nord-Ouest 1795-1803, Port Napoléon 1803); the British took the island in 1810 and Governor Robert Farquhar restored the name Port Louis.

source.title: History - City Council Of Port Louis (History of the City)
source.quote: In 1810, Governor Robert Farquhar restored the name Port Louis. (summary of page text)

places.name: Central Market (Bazaar central)
places.what: The main market of Port Louis, with fish, meat, grocery and fresh produce sections. Its present layout dates from the 1845 building, with later reconstruction after fires.

facts.label: Origin of market sales
facts.value: First fruit and vegetable sales were held in front of St Louis Cathedral in 1773.

source.title: STREET VENDORS – PART II: Our findings in the Central Market of Port-Louis…
source.quote: 1773 ... St Louis Cathedral (summarised)

facts.label: Fire of 1816
facts.value: A fire destroyed the market on 25 September 1816.

source.title: STREET VENDORS – PART II: Our findings in the Central Market of Port-Louis…
source.quote: 25 September 1816 fire (summarised)

facts.label: Building
facts.value: Bazaar central built in 1845 with four wings; fish and meat wings survived to 2012 without major repairs.

source.title: STREET VENDORS – PART II: Our findings in the Central Market of Port-Louis…
source.quote: 167 years without major repairs

facts.label: Later fires and reconstruction
facts.value: Fires destroyed the grocery section (19 May 1981) and vegetable section (4 November 1999); reconstruction completed 11 March 2004.

source.title: STREET VENDORS – PART II: Our findings in the Central Market of Port-Louis…
source.quote: (summarised from page)

places.name: Champ de Mars Racecourse
places.what: A racecourse in the centre of Port Louis, where horse racing began in 1812 on a former military training ground. It is home to the Mauritius Turf Club.

facts.label: First races
facts.value: First racing day 25 June 1812.

source.title: PUBLICATION ET EXPOSITION: Au rythme de 200 ans de courses hippiques
source.quote: first racing day 25 June 1812 (summarised)

facts.label: Oldest in southern hemisphere
facts.value: Le Mauricien calls it the first racecourse of the southern hemisphere.

source.title: PUBLICATION ET EXPOSITION: Au rythme de 200 ans de courses hippiques
source.quote: le premier hippodrome de l'hémisphère sud

facts.label: Purpose
facts.value: Governor Farquhar organised races to bring English and French communities together; the site was a former French military training ground.

source.title: Two centuries on, racing fervour still unites Mauritians
source.author: AFP (no individual author)
source.quote: 200-year-old track in the centre of Port Louis (summarised)

facts.label: Club ranking (disputed)
facts.value: AFP: the club is 'believed to be the third oldest racing club in the world'; other web sources say second. Do not state a world rank.

source.title: Two centuries on, racing fervour still unites Mauritians
source.author: AFP (no individual author)
source.quote: believed to be the third oldest racing club in the world

places.name: The Citadel (Fort Adelaide)
places.what: A basalt fort on a hill above Port Louis, built by the British in the 1830s. It is a national monument and a viewpoint over the city.

facts.label: Construction
facts.value: Built 1834-1840 at about 40,000 pounds sterling, then the most expensive construction on the island; named after Queen Adelaide.

source.title: Economic Development Board : appel à candidatures international pour «régénérer» La Citadelle
source.author: Patrick Hilbert
source.quote: Construction began in 1834 and finished in 1840 (summarised)

facts.label: Workforce
facts.value: Convicts from India, indentured Indian workers, Mauritian prisoners, craftsmen from Bombay and local masons.

source.title: Economic Development Board : appel à candidatures international pour «régénérer» La Citadelle
source.author: Patrick Hilbert
source.quote: (summarised from page)

facts.label: Purpose
facts.value: Built to house British troops and watch for unrest before the abolition of slavery; never used much in practice.

source.title: La Citadelle, a museum in the making
source.author: Dominique Bellier
source.quote: used only for rare temporary mobilizations (summarised)

facts.label: Heritage status
facts.value: Declared a national monument in 1958 (Government Notice No. 614).

source.title: Economic Development Board : appel à candidatures international pour «régénérer» La Citadelle
source.author: Patrick Hilbert
source.quote: (summarised from page)

places.name: Jummah Mosque
places.what: A large mosque in the middle of Chinatown in central Port Louis. It grew from a small mosque on land bought in 1852 into the present building.

facts.label: Founding
facts.value: Founded 1852 when a small Muslim community acquired land in the city centre.

source.title: Jummah Mosque : un havre de quiétude au cœur de la capitale
source.quote: fondée en 1852 (summarised)

facts.label: Government listing
facts.value: Ministry of Tourism: 'built in the 1850's, in the middle of Chinatown'.

source.title: Tourist Sites
source.publisher: Ministry of Tourism, Government of Mauritius
source.quote: visit Port Louis' Jummah Mosque, built in the 1850's, in the middle of Chinatown

facts.label: Wooden staircase
facts.value: Entirely wooden spiral staircase, once used by the muezzin to call to prayer.

source.title: Jummah Mosque : un havre de quiétude au cœur de la capitale
source.quote: (summarised from page)

facts.label: Size
facts.value: Around 3,000 people pass through for Friday prayers and big occasions.

source.title: Jummah Mosque : un havre de quiétude au cœur de la capitale
source.quote: (summarised)

places.name: Natural History Museum (Mauritius Institute)
places.what: The oldest museum in Mauritius, housed in the Mauritius Institute building. It shows 500 years of the island's natural history, with a dodo model as centrepiece. Status of reopening after the 2017 closure was not confirmed.

facts.label: Opening
facts.value: Desjardins Museum opened to the public on 14 October 1842.

source.title: Historical Background (Natural History Museum)
source.quote: On 14 October 1842, the Desjardins Museum was opened to the public.

facts.label: Move
facts.value: In 1885 the collection moved to the new Mauritius Institute building.

source.title: Historical Background (Natural History Museum)
source.quote: In 1885, the collection of Desjardins Museum was transferred to the newly erected Mauritius Institute Building.

facts.label: National museum
facts.value: Proclaimed a National museum in 2000.

source.title: Historical Background (Natural History Museum)
source.quote: In 2000, the Natural History Museum of the Mauritius Institute was proclaimed a National museum.

facts.label: Dodo
facts.value: Dodo model is the centrepiece; the skeleton on display was collected in 1900, all bones from one bird.

source.title: About The Museum (Natural History Museum)
source.quote: A model of the Dodo, the centrepiece of the museum, is displayed in this gallery.
